# Pasting images into TextInput should not be this hard
![Arunabh Verma](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/9r24npb8/production/f4c80db2ce7988e62548c0c8ed34b82660fa4d11-400x400.jpg?auto=format&fit=max&q=75&w=48)

Arunabh Verma

Guest Author

[Bluesky](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Pasting%20images%20into%20TextInput%20should%20not%20be%20this%20hard%20https%3A%2F%2Fexpo.dev%2Fblog%2Fpasting-images-into-textinput-should-not-be-this-hard)[X](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Pasting%20images%20into%20TextInput%20should%20not%20be%20this%20hard%20https%3A%2F%2Fexpo.dev%2Fblog%2Fpasting-images-into-textinput-should-not-be-this-hard)[Reddit](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexpo.dev%2Fblog%2Fpasting-images-into-textinput-should-not-be-this-hard&title=Pasting%20images%20into%20TextInput%20should%20not%20be%20this%20hard)[Y Combinator](https://news.ycombinator.com/submitlink?u=https%3A%2F%2Fexpo.dev%2Fblog%2Fpasting-images-into-textinput-should-not-be-this-hard&t=Pasting%20images%20into%20TextInput%20should%20not%20be%20this%20hard)[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexpo.dev%2Fblog%2Fpasting-images-into-textinput-should-not-be-this-hard)

![Pasting images into TextInput should not be this hard](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/9r24npb8/production/2719b7938b17350b92d9b8c4168226378e39b41a-2400x1350.png?auto=format&fit=max&q=75&w=1200)

[**Powstać**](https://powstac.com/) was building a chat application.

But one tiny interaction was missing: Copy an image, tap the chat input, and paste it.

As a user, this feels obvious. Native apps do it all the time. You copy a screenshot, a meme, a GIF, or an image from another app, paste it into the composer, and it appears as an attachment. No file picker, no extra taps, no ceremony. Just paste.

So I decided to add it.

## Building a new input wasn't the answer
It supports rich content editing and embedded media, which is powerful.

When a user pastes an image into a chat application, I do not necessarily want that image inserted into the input itself. I want the image file.

That distinction ended up becoming the whole point.

## iOS
So the wrapper only reads from `UIPasteboard` after the user explicitly performs a paste action.

Once the paste happens, the native layer inspects the clipboard contents: text, images, GIFs, WebP, HEIC, and anything else useful.

The payload stays intentionally small:

Copy

That gave me the API I wanted from the beginning: a paste event that lets the app decide what to do next.

## Android was much harder
- paste text → text appears

But making that feel native takes work. If the clipboard contains media, the wrapper should intercept it, save the content into cache storage, and emit file URIs back to JavaScript.

## The edge cases never end
- multiple images
- GIFs
- transparent PNGs
- screenshots pasted directly from the system screenshot UI

Each one behaved a little differently.

GIFs needed to remain GIFs instead of accidentally becoming static images.

Screenshots were another surprise. Images copied from the Photos app behaved differently from screenshots copied directly from the system screenshot UI.

## The result
- text paste
- image paste
- multiple image paste
- GIF paste
- screenshots
- iOS stickers
- animated stickers

## Final thoughts
Behind a single **Paste** button sits clipboard privacy, temporary files, GIF handling, Android content APIs, native text editing systems, image formats, stickers, screenshots, and platform-specific behavior that users never think about.

Which is exactly why it matters. Users should not have to think about any of it. They should just copy something, paste it, and move on.

If you are building a chat application, social platform, notes app, AI application, or any workflow where users frequently share media, give [`expo-paste-input`](https://github.com/arunabhverma/expo-paste-input) a try. And if you find an edge case I have not discovered yet, I would love to hear about it.
